gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns applying a finite-horizon tracking estimate without proving that perturbed trajectories remain in the domain K=[−1,1]. ISSUE-001 instead concerns an invalid finite-limit-set argument and failure to establish convergence to a stationary limit; it does not diagnose the missing trajectory-domain hypothesis or uniform-continuity premise.

The gold issue is an equality-case gap in the rank-1 approximation boundary-inward proposition, involving r_t=0 and 4‖a_t‖²−δ=0. ISSUE-002 identifies a scalar certificate endpoint failure at δ=η, with a different certificate, parameter endpoint, and monotonicity/stationarity claim.

The gold issue concerns overstating finite-horizon numerical norm growth as asymptotic unboundedness. ISSUE-001 concerns a theoretical convergence proof gap and contains no diagnosis of the empirical finite-versus-asymptotic inference.

Both identify the scalar endpoint δ=η=δ_th as invalid for the claimed equality-only-at-stationary property: the scalar remainder vanishes there, so a nonstationary boundary point can have zero certificate change. Both recognize that the endpoint must be excluded or the stationarity/uniqueness assertion weakened.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The scalar certificate's endpoint δ=η has zero one-step remainder at nonstationary boundary points, so the claimed strict stationarity characterization and closed-endpoint uniqueness conclusion are unsupported.

component_coverage.gold_component: At the canonical threshold δ_th(η)=η, a nonstationary certificate-boundary point has zero one-step certificate change, contradicting equality only at stationary points.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 explicitly gives the scalar endpoint δ=η, the vanishing remainder, and equality at nonstationary boundary points.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proof does not establish the theorem's closed endpoint and must restrict the stationarity/uniqueness claim to the open range or weaken the endpoint claim.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 states that the abstract-framework verification fails at δ=η and proposes moving the threshold above η or restricting the relevant axiom to the open interval.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the missing level-coverage argument: a local Lagrange calculation applies only when a level set contains an appropriate unbalanced global minimizer, but the proof does not establish that every arbitrary nonterminal level has one. Both also recognize that the claimed sweep of the canonical minimizer parameter cannot by itself prove uniqueness for an arbitrary admissible family.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The uniqueness proof fails to establish coverage of every arbitrary nonterminal level by an unbalanced global minimizer/ellipse before applying the local calculation; therefore global uniqueness does not follow from the canonical minimizer parameterization alone.

component_coverage.gold_component: The local quadratic-form/Lagrange calculation is conditional on a nonterminal boundary containing an unbalanced global minimizer, and the proof does not establish that premise for every arbitrary level.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 explicitly states that the calculation applies only when such a minimizer exists and that coverage of every level is not shown.

component_coverage.gold_component: Without the missing coverage step, the conclusion of global uniqueness across all nonterminal levels is unsupported.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 identifies the resulting incompleteness of the uniqueness theorem and supplies the needed nesting/continuity bridge.

component_coverage.gold_component: A repair must show terminal exclusion and use nesting/continuity to cover or identify every level set, rather than infer coverage from the canonical parameter range alone.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 proposes a lemma excluding unbalanced minimizers from the terminal set and a nesting/continuity argument showing all relevant level sets are represented by the canonical ellipses.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both provide an increasing reparameterization counterexample showing that the axioms preserve the nested level-set family but do not determine the numerical parameterization P(δ) on the original δ-scale. Both repair the theorem by weakening uniqueness to uniqueness up to increasing reparameterization.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The axioms are invariant under increasing changes of the state coordinate, so they cannot uniquely determine the numerical family P(δ) without an additional normalization; only the level-set family, or P up to reparameterization, is identified.

component_coverage.gold_component: An admissible increasing reparameterization produces a different numerical P(δ) while preserving the axioms and structural properties.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 explicitly gives the reparameterization invariance and concludes that P is not numerically unique at each δ.

component_coverage.gold_component: The displayed ellipsoid family remains distinguished only as a level-set family, not as a uniquely parameterized P(δ).
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 states that uniqueness of the family of level sets survives while literal numerical uniqueness fails.

component_coverage.gold_component: The theorem must be restated up to increasing reparameterization, with an additional normalization required to identify the original coordinate.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 supplies the same corrected theorem and normalization qualification.
